source: scripts/ops/score-ops.mjs over data/ee/ GeoTIFFs (0.1° grid); criteria in scripts/ops/tasks.mjs; method in docs/estrategias-bases.md
proxies: ps_hpa estimated from elevation (standard atmosphere) until MERRA-2 surface pressure is available
dust_aod and wind_ms (MERRA-2) not available yet: dust criteria are skipped

tasks.name: Spacesuit EVA on cold, rough, thin-air terrain
tasks.need: Suit mobility, fatigue and procedures on broken, bare terrain, in the cold and at low pressure (less oxygen, like a pressurised suit with a low-pressure mix).

criteria.why: Night-time cold below −40 °C stresses suits, gloves and batteries
Rough but walkable ground (5 km slope)
Thin air: below ~600 hPa means above ~4 km altitude

tasks.name: Navigation and operations under low-angle sun and long shadows
tasks.need: At the lunar south pole the Sun stays within ~1.5° of the horizon: long shadows, glare and spots where cameras and people go blind. Navigation, rover driving and solar panels on vertical masts.

criteria.why: Polar latitude: the Sun circles low over the horizon (polar day and night)
Snow-free ground in summer (regolith, not ice)

tasks.name: Hardware and EVA in extreme cold (permanently shadowed craters)
tasks.need: Shackleton's shadowed floor stays below −230 °C, colder than anywhere on Earth. Earth can only test the start of that curve: seals, lubricants, batteries and short EVAs at −60 °C or below.

criteria.why: The colder the better, up to Earth's p1 (−75 °C)
Even the summer maximum stays cold

tasks.name: Drilling and extracting shallow ground ice
tasks.need: Arcadia has water ice under less than 1 m of soil (SWIM). Shackleton has ice in permanently shadowed regolith. Drilling, sampling ice-cemented ground and extracting water (ISRU).

criteria.why: Mean annual surface temperature well below 0 °C (continuous-permafrost proxy)

gaps: We have no direct ground-ice or permafrost layer: ESA CCI Permafrost (ground temperature and probability, Obu et al. 2019) would replace the proxy.

tasks.name: Operations with dust: abrasion, seals and panel cleaning
tasks.need: Martian dust is fine and electrostatic, and dust storms cut solar power (Opportunity, 2018). Testing seals, filters, airlocks and panel cleaning.

criteria.why: Aridity: dust is not washed out
Loose, bright sediment (not rock, not ice)
Hot surface: convection and dust devils lift dust (as on Mars)

tasks.proxyNote: Without MERRA-2 dust and wind, the task falls back to aridity and loose sediment only.

tasks.name: Landing and launch: pad, plume and ejected debris
tasks.need: Engine plumes dig craters and throw regolith (Apollo 12, Chang'e). Testing pads, berms and hazard detection.

criteria.why: Sediment or rock, not water or ice

tasks.name: Deploying power in cold, dusty, thin air (solar + fission)
tasks.need: On Mars sunlight is ~43 % of Earth's, dust covers the panels and the cold eats batteries. Deploying panels, cables and a small reactor mock-up (Fission Surface Power).

criteria.why: Thin air: less convective cooling, like Mars
Dust that dims and soils panels (MERRA-2)

tasks.name: Building with regolith (sintering, 3D printing, berms)
tasks.need: Shielding against radiation and micrometeorites with local material: dark basaltic soil is the closest feedstock to lunar and Martian simulants.
gaps: Albedo does not distinguish basalt from other dark rock: ASTER GED (emissivity, silica index) would say whether it is truly basaltic. Shackleton's highlands are anorthositic (bright): there, dark ground is NOT the right analog.

tasks.name: Long-distance rover traverses
tasks.need: Perseverance-style traverses: tens of km over plains and delta sediment, with autonomous navigation and communications relay.
tasks.windowNote: Score averaged over a 7 × 7-cell window (~75 km): the favourable terrain has to be continuous for a long traverse.

tasks.name: Crew isolation and delayed communications
tasks.need: Psychology, autonomy and procedures with no quick help (HERA, CHAPEA, Concordia). The communication delay (2.6 s Moon; 4–24 min Mars) is simulated anywhere; remoteness is not.

criteria.why: More than a day from the nearest city

tasks.name: Astrobiology sampling in hyper-arid sediments
tasks.need: Jezero is an ancient lake delta. Testing contamination-free sampling, caching and life detection at the dry limit of life (Atacama, Mars 2020).
gaps: We have no lacustrine or deltaic geology layer: a dry-lake map (Global Lakes and Wetlands Database, playas) would separate deltas and salars from rocky desert.
